definition: Semantic mapping (SM) is a statistical method for dimensionality reduction (the transformation of data from a high-dimensional space into a low-dimensional space).
details: SM can be used in a set of multidimensional vectors of features to extract a few new features that preserves the main data characteristics. SM performs dimensionality reduction by clustering the original features in semantic clusters and combining features mapped in the same cluster to generate an extracted feature. Given a data set, this method constructs a projection matrix that can be used to map a data element from a high-dimensional space into a reduced dimensional space. SM can be applied in construction of text mining and information retrieval systems, as well as systems managing vectors of high dimensionality. SM is an alternative to random mapping, principal components analysis and latent semantic indexing methods.

explainer.lead: Semantic mapping is a statistical dimensionality-reduction method that clusters original features into semantic clusters and combines the features within each cluster into new extracted features. It matters because it keeps the main data characteristics while shrinking the feature space.

tiers.eli5: It groups similar measurements together and replaces each group with one summary number.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to multidimensional feature vectors to reduce dimensions by constructing a projection matrix that maps data into the lower-dimensional space. A pitfall is that clustering quality drives the result: features lumped into the wrong semantic cluster yield extracted features that no longer preserve the main characteristics.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a data set, semantic mapping performs dimensionality reduction by clustering the original features in semantic clusters, combining features mapped in the same cluster to generate an extracted feature, and constructing a projection matrix that maps a data element from a high-dimensional space into a reduced dimensional space. Its limit is that feature preservation depends on the quality of the semantic clustering.

explainer.example: From a set of multidimensional feature vectors, semantic mapping clusters correlated features, combines each cluster into one extracted feature, and builds a projection matrix that maps new vectors into the reduced space.
